notes: Summary: Pyxis is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for high-throughput product recommendation and chat features across NA/EU markets.
Business driver: reduce per-request latency for personalization while lowering per-token cost vs current self-hosted fleet.
Key ask: contractual minimum throughput (tokens/sec) + deterministic concurrency caps and a predictable burst policy.

Traffic profile: baseline sustained traffic ~60k tokens/sec across model endpoints (embeddings + reranker + chat). Peak spikes to ~180k tokens/sec during flash-sales events (3-4x baseline) for windows of 30-90 mins.
Latency SLO: P95 generation latency target <= 120 ms for request prompt+completion up to 256 tokens; P99 target <= 300 ms with contiguous burst buffers.
Throughput guarantee proposal from Redwood (discussed 2026-02-14):
- Reserved compute footprint: 12x LGA-class GPUs (customer recommended A100-80GB equivalents) with dedicated pools per route.
- Contracted min tokens/sec (sustained): 25,000 tokens/sec across reserved cluster (measured at model output tokens/sec by route weightings).
- Concurrency caps: hard cap of 400 concurrent requests across the cluster for interactive chat endpoints; 600 concurrent streams for lower-latency embedding jobs (configurable).
- Burst policy: 2.5x over contracted tokens/sec for up to 45 minutes per 24h rolling window; automatic throttling to kept-alive queue after burst budget exhausted.
- Mixed routing: critical routes pinned to reserved pool; lower-priority background jobs routed to best-effort pooled capacity with fallback to hosted API during bursts.
Customer feedback on initial proposal (call 2026-02-14):
- "Need absolute guarantee on min tokens/sec during EU flash sales window; local residency required." — VP Eng
- Concern about '2.5x for 45 minutes' — wants a tiered burst policy (short high-burst 5x for 5 mins then 2x for remainder).
- Wants explicit billing model for burst consumption vs sustained capacity (prepaid burst credits vs usage-based).
Security asks: architecture diagram showing KMS integration, audit log retention 1 year, SAML metadata exchange tests scheduled.
Procurement ask: SLA language that ties financial remedies to failure to meet contracted min tokens/sec for a rolling hour window (not just monthly availability).
Action items from last call:
- Redwood to return revised SLA appendix with tiered burst buckets and explicit measurement methodology (owner: Maya, due 2026-03-05).
- SE (Owen) to produce throughput validation plan (load script + test harness) and run a two-week soak POC against customer staging (target start 2026-03-10).
- Customer security team to provide KMS network constraints and confirmed VPC peering window (due 2026-03-02).
POC specifics discussed:
- POC targets: demonstrate sustained 30k tokens/sec at configured latency SLO for 7 consecutive days and a 5-minute 150k tokens/sec spike with <10% error rate.
- Measurement: use token-metering hooks at request ingress + per-model output verification; Redwood to share sample telemetry query (Grafana/PromQL).
Risks:
- If burst billing unclear, legal will push to shorter contract or higher reserve commitment.
- On-prem KMS tight network restrictions may increase integration timeline by 3-4 weeks.
Quote: "We need predictable tail behavior. If Redwood can't guarantee minimum sustained throughput during sales, we'll keep the lucky-charm self-host fleet for peak windows." — Head of Product
Internal AE notes: exec sponsor introduced (CPO) — good for accelerating procurement but wants explicit runway on cost cadence.
